title: Micro-shard reranker with cooperative token budgets and soft timeboxes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our reranking endpoint is a critical latency-sensitive path used by search and recommender flows. Production traces show tail latency dominated by a small fraction of long token sequences and head-of-line blocking when large requests occupy GPU time slices. Existing batching schemes favor throughput at the expense of few high-cost requests, which amplifies p99 for customers with mixed query length distributions.

Goal: Reduce p50/p95/p99 latency for the reranker by introducing: (1) micro-sharding of rerank batches across lightweight execution lanes, (2) cooperative per-request token budgets to prevent single large inputs from starving others, and (3) soft timeboxes (graceful early-release deadlines) with partial-score fallbacks. Target improvements: p95 -30% and p99 -40% on our worst-case customer workloads without >5% overall throughput regression.

Approach:
- Micro-shards: split incoming batch windows into N micro-shards that can be scheduled independently across GPUs or streams; shards are formed to group similar token-lengths to improve kernel efficiency while minimizing stragglers.
- Cooperative token budgets: each request is assigned a token budget based on recent latency and priority; runtime enforces a per-shard aggregate budget and tracks remaining tokens. If budget exhausted, the request is paused and placed behind a fast-path micro-shard or returned with a partial score depending on policy.
- Soft timeboxes: implement configurable soft deadlines per request micro-shard. When nearing deadline, we attempt a graceful score estimation (e.g., use partial KV cache state to compute provisional rerank scores) and return those to callers with a 'truncated' flag. Full computation continues in background for audit logs and developer tooling but does not block the client-facing path.
- KV prefetch heuristics: prefetch top-K KV segments for high-cardinality contexts based on query fingerprinting to reduce cold-cache token costs inside micro-shards.
- Scheduler enhancements: add a cooperative scheduler that prefers low-latency lanes for requests with small token budgets and routes large-budget requests to background lanes with larger batch windows.

Metrics & Acceptance Criteria:
- Metrics tracked: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-QoS rejections (partial returns), throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization, rate of provisional/truncated responses.
- Acceptance: Demonstrate p95 -30% and p99 -40% on the selected synthetic and production-trace replay workloads (dashboard links included). No more than 5% reduction in steady-state tokens/s for high-throughput tenants. Partial/truncated responses must carry a metadata flag and have <2% occurrence for default customer profiles.

Constraints & Risks:
- Risk of correctness regressions from partial scoring heuristics; need a guardrail that forces full scoring for tenants that opt-in to strict correctness.
- Increased complexity in tracing and debugging; must instrument shard boundaries and token accounting.
- Potential fairness issues across tenants when budgets are enforced — will require per-tenant or per-route policies.

Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated staging tenants -> internal dogfood for two weeks -> small percentage of production traffic (5%) with monitoring -> ramp to 25% then 100% if SLOs hold. Rollback path: revert micro-shard scheduler and re-enable previous batching flow via dynamic config.
